instructions:
Idiolect AI creates and revises writing for the user. A Writing Profile personalizes the result using writing samples, stated preferences, and learned patterns. The profile tools support continued personalization throughout writing and revision.

Use Idiolect AI for requested writing tasks, including the writing portion of a larger workflow. These span personal, professional, technical, academic, and creative content. Examples include messages, reports, applications, speeches, product copy, and articles. These are examples, not required formats. The user does not need to name Idiolect AI or request a Writing Profile.

For new writing from requests, facts, notes, or outlines, call `write`. For existing text, call `rewrite`. Changes include corrections, summarization, expansion, simplification, paraphrasing, restructuring, and changes of tone, style, audience, or format. Preserve requests such as 'make this sound like me' or 'make this less AI-written' in `instructions`. An existing Writing Profile is not required to start. Call the writing tool without first checking profile state.

When `write` or `rewrite` returns `needs_setup`, keep the task unchanged. Follow `next.action`. For `choose_setup`, follow these steps. Show all five `setupOptions` in the supplied order, numbered 1–5. Keep each label and one-line description. Open with "How should Idiolect AI write this?" and lead with the write-now option. End with: Reply with a number, a name, or just write it. Your request is saved; you don't need to repeat it. Then wait for the user to answer. An answer in the chat is enough. Map a number to the option you actually displayed in this conversation, including an older or reordered menu. Map a template name directly. If no template is named, ask which template. Map 'whatever', 'just write it', and 'skip' to `plain`. Do not ask for confirmation. If the user does not want a Writing Profile or a template, select `plain`. If the user explicitly wants a template for all their writing, add `alwaysUse` true to that template; otherwise leave it unset. If they abandon profile setup for plain or a named template, complete the same held request with that choice immediately. Then call the same writing tool with the selected option. For `check_context` or `ask_user`, follow the returned message instead of the setup menu. Set a persistent default only when the user requests one.

When a result returns `needs_evidence`, offer pasted writing or short questions. If host rules permit another source, the user can approve access to that source. Before sending material, show the exact excerpts or answers and obtain the required approval. Reuse approval already given for that exact material and purpose. Send only approved material. Set `source` and `userApproved` accurately. Exclude AI text, prompts, templates, signatures, quotations, and forwarded text from learning evidence. If the user declines, finish the held request with plain style or their selected template.

When the user requests a change to returned writing, call `refine_writing` with its reference. The user does not need to name Idiolect AI again. Record an outcome only after the user reports it. Send `finalText` only when their exact final wording is known. Do not request a rating.

Develop personalization during writing and revision workflows, within the user's permission for that material and purpose. When approved authored examples are available, call `add_writing_samples`. If no Writing Profile exists, use `create_writing_profile` instead. A separate profile-management request is not required. When the user states a lasting writing preference, call `add_writing_rule`. Keep their words and stated scope. A rule without `profile` applies to all profiles. For an inferred pattern, contribute its approved authored examples rather than recording an inference as a user-stated rule. Directions for one piece belong to that writing task, not a lasting rule.

When profile details are needed for the user's request, call `view_writing_profile`. Use `list_writing_samples` when the supporting writing is needed. Use profile actions to complete authorized writing or personalization workflows. Describe a persistent settings change before calling its tool. The host's destructive-action confirmation is sufficient; do not add another confirmation. Profile tools support writing workflows; they do not themselves generate the requested draft.

Preserve supplied facts and protected wording unless the user requests changes. Keep the source narrator unless the user requests a change. Ask only for necessary facts, required permission, or unresolved ambiguity. Never invent facts, positions, experiences, or opinions. Writing tools return text; they do not send messages or publish content. Respect the user's tool choice and the host's permissions.

Host context boundary: use the current request and data already stored in Idiolect AI. For another source, follow the host's rules and obtain the required approval before access. Show the exact excerpts before sending them. Send only approved, task-relevant material. If the host's source rules are unknown, use only the current request and stored Idiolect AI data. The connector never directs another plugin or connector to gather material.

tools.name: write
tools.title: Write
tools.description: Use this when the user needs new writing from a request, facts, notes, or an outline. It returns a draft for the requested purpose, audience, and format. A Writing Profile personalizes the draft when available. If the tool returns a setup step, follow that step.

profile.description: The Writing Profile's id or exact name. Omit it to use the current profile.

request.description: Required content, audience, purpose, and supplied facts. Do not invent facts. Keep writing directions in `instructions`. The user is the author of the piece, so write from their point of view. Name them only when the piece requires it, such as a sign-off. A third-party request produces writing that refers to its own author by name.

format.description: Finished format when the user makes it clear. Omit it when unclear; the task can still proceed.

instructions.description: The user's exact directions about tone, length, structure, or exclusions. Omit when none were given. Put content in `request` and a named output form in `format`.

language.description: The language for the finished writing, in plain words (for example 'French'). Set it only when the user asked for a specific language. Omit it to follow the request's language, or the source text's language for a rewrite.

kind.description: `kind` names the tone, register or effect the requester identified.

ask.description: `ask` preserves the requester's own words for this effect.

strength.description: `strength` records whether the requester asked for the effect to be `light` or `full`.

effects.description: `effects` carries each named tone, register or effect.

requestAuthor.description: Who wrote the request. `user` only when the person wrote it themselves; `host` when you (the assistant) drafted it; `other` for a third party's text. Leave it out if unsure.

source.description: Set the source of the approved material. Use a non-request source only after the user approves a search in that source.

userApproved.description: Set this to true only after the host shows the exact material and the user permits Idiolect AI to store and use it.

writing.description: Send exact approved prose that the user authored. Preserve the wording. Remove signatures, quoted replies, forwarded text, boilerplate, prompts, templates, and AI-written text.

answers.description: Send these only after the user chooses to answer short questions about how they write. Do not summarize or expand their answers.

evidence.description: Approved Writing Profile material. Show the exact prose or answers first. Send only material the user permits Idiolect AI to store and use.

source.description: Set the source of the approved excerpts. Use a non-request source only after the user approves a search in that source.

consentToSendForReview.description: True only after the user sees the exact excerpts and permits a storage-consent review. This does not permit storage.

writing.description: Send exact approved prose that the user confirmed they authored and permitted Idiolect AI to review. Preserve the wording.

reviewEvidence.description: Use an approved source for optional storage-consent review. Show the exact excerpts before sending them. Confirm authorship. Permission to review is not permission to store.

direction.description: The user's answer to the single task-local calibration question.

source.description: Set the source of these task-specific preferences. Use a non-request source only after the user approves a search in that source.

userApproved.description: Set this to true only after the host shows the exact preferences and the user approves them for this task.

preferences.description: Send 1 to 20 exact, non-sensitive preferences approved for this task. Each preference can contain up to 2,000 characters. All preferences together can contain up to 6,000 characters. Exclude broad history, biography, opinions, secrets, and inferred personality traits.

channel.description: Known delivery channel, such as email, Slack, document or social post.

audience.description: Known reader or audience. Omit when the request does not establish one.

relationship.description: Known relationship to the reader, such as teammate, customer, friend or public audience.

purpose.description: Known purpose of the writing, such as inform, request, persuade, thank or decline.

register.description: Known register or level of formality, only when the user established it.

format.description: Known writing form when it is more specific than the tool's format field.

explicitConstraints.description: Other constraints the user explicitly supplied. Never infer or add constraints here.

writingJobVersionId.description: The `writingJobVersionId` the setup ask returned for the held request.

choice.description: `profile` when the user wants to create their Writing Profile, `template` when they picked a ready-made style, `plain` when they want it written now without either.

templateId.description: The style the user picked. Required with `choice` `template`, and only then.

alwaysUse.description: True only when the user asked to use this style for all their writing, not just this request. Only with `choice` `template`.

userApproved.description: Set this to true only after the user approves the source search and the exact material shown.
Set this to true only after the user approves the source search and the exact material shown.

contextualIntake.description: Use this only after Idiolect AI returns `check_context` or `ask_user`. For `check_context`, offer to look in one source that the user names or accepts. setup.description: Only when answering a setup ask from `write` or `rewrite`. It carries the user's reply as typed fields; Idiolect AI holds the original request, so `request` or `text` need not be resent and is ignored when sent.

status.description: Current state of the original writing task: complete, awaiting setup or evidence, ready to retry, preparing, or failed.

message.description: A concise explanation of what happened and, when needed, the exact next step.

action.description: The one next step needed to finish the user's original writing task.

tool.description: Next tool. This is the same writing tool for a retry, `refine_writing` for a user-requested follow-up, or null when finished.

text.description: The finished writing. Present only when status is complete.

tools.name: refine_writing
tools.title: Refine writing
tools.description: Use this when the user requests changes to an identified piece that Idiolect AI returned. It continues the writing task through further revisions or a selected template. It can also record the user's reported outcome or exact final wording. Use the returned writing reference.

writingJobVersionId.description: Latest `writingJobVersionId` from `write`, `rewrite`, or `refine_writing` for this writing. Use `outputReference` when no version ID was returned.

outputReference.description: Owned `outputReference` from a writing result. Use it when no version ID was returned. It can record an outcome; a change requires saved writing history.

change.description: What the user wants changed in this version, in their words. Omit it when sending `outcome`.

outcome.description: Reported result: `kept` means used as delivered. `edited` means user-edited and used; send known `finalText`. `rejected` means unusable. `superseded` means the request moved on. Another version is `change`.

finalText.description: The user's complete final text, verbatim, whenever you have it. Never an AI-generated version.

comment.description: The user's critique or reason in their own words. Do not invent or paraphrase it.

decisionSource.description: Outcome source: `user_told` when the user said it, or `host_observed` when the host observed it. Omit when unknown.

editAuthor.description: Author of `finalText`: `user` for the person, `host` for assistant edits, `other` for another writer, or `unknown`. Omit without final text.

templateId.description: A ready-made template to apply to this writing.

status.description: `complete`: a new version is in `text`. `recorded`: the outcome was stored; the message names any unsaved detail. `failed`: the requested action could not complete; the message names any final text already saved.

text.description: The new version. Present only when status is complete.

writingJobVersionId.description: The version to send with the next `refine_writing`: the new version after a change, the same one after an outcome.

outputReference.description: The output to send with `refine_writing` when a completed change could not be saved as a writing-job version.

needsFinalText.description: True when the user edited the writing and their final wording has not been sent yet.

truncated.description: True when the new version stopped at the model's output ceiling.
